audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 exposure includes $343 million of earnings attributable to noncontrolling interests, $898 million of consolidated D&A and $950 million of consolidated capital expenditures
audit_findings.mechanism: The owner-earnings numerator starts with parent-attributable earnings but applies consolidated D&A, capital-spending and other cash-flow adjustments before dividing by CF common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: For financial reporting purposes, the assets, liabilities and earnings of CFN and the Blue Point joint venture are consolidated into our financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, although its net direction is unresolved. Non-parent D&A add-backs could overstate OE, while deductions for capital spending funded by noncontrolling partners could understate OE. The affected filed amounts are large relative to the $1,723.2 million anchor and therefore reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild FY2025 OE by legal entity, allocating CFN and Blue Point D&A, capital expenditures, other adjustments and distributions consistently with parent-attributable earnings, then rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may add cash that CF common holders do not own or cannot use
audit_findings.magnitude: $341 million of June 2026 Blue Point cash is restricted to Blue Point obligations; excluding all of it reduces value by $2.23 per share, or 1.3% of the $174.45 base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated cash is added dollar-for-dollar to the equity bridge even when it is restricted inside the Blue Point VIE or partly supports CFN's noncontrolling interest.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, all assets of the Blue Point joint venture can only be used to settle the obligations of the Blue Point joint venture.
audit_findings.explanation: The demonstrated Blue Point exposure is too small by itself to change the conclusion: removing the entire $341 million, a more conservative treatment than merely removing the partners' 60% share, reduces the base value to about $172.22 per share and the buy-below level by about $1.56, versus the existing $11.24 gap between the $133.35 price and $122.11 buy-below level. Any CFN cash allocation remains unquantified and should still be reconciled.
audit_findings.action: Replace consolidated cash with legally available parent cash by entity, excluding all Blue Point restricted cash and allocating CFN cash consistently with CHS's rights; rerun the equity bridge to confirm the bounded effect.

audit_findings.title: Committed Blue Point investment may be missing from the forecast
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $1.61-$1.65 billion of remaining parent funding, computed from 40% of the $3.7 billion facility cost less $351 million of contributions through June 2026, plus approximately $482 million of the $550 million Common Facilities cost remaining after $68 million spent
audit_findings.mechanism: Future parent-funded construction cash outflows are omitted from forecast OE or the equity bridge while low-carbon benefits may enter forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate that the cost of the low-carbon ATR ammonia production facility with CCS technologies will be approximately $3.7 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The remaining commitment is approximately $10.53-$10.81 per diluted share before discounting, taxes, cost changes or offsetting project value. audit_findings.title: FY2025 is not a clean forward run-rate anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified valuation effect; 2026 gross-ammonia guidance of 9.5 million tons is 620,000 tons, or 6.1%, below 2025 production of 10.120 million tons, while 2025 selling-price increases added approximately $1.06 billion of revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor is carried into every scenario, including the zero-growth bear case, without an explicit 2026 outage adjustment or commodity-cycle normalization.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect gross ammonia production for 2026 will be approximately 9.5 million tons reflecting a decrease from 2025 due in part to the outage at our Yazoo City complex.
audit_findings.explanation: The production shortfall and unusually favorable 2025 pricing are demonstrated, but their net earnings effect cannot be established because 2026 prices may offset lower volume and the Yazoo outage is temporary. Since the full $1,723.2 million anchor is compounded and terminalized, a plausible normalization could materially change value.
audit_findings.action: Construct a normalized parent-attributable OE anchor using filed 2026 volume guidance, the expected Yazoo recovery schedule, normalized product prices and natural-gas costs; separately show a bridge from reported FY2025 OE and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Noncash supply-contract liability amortization may be treated as cash earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $30 million in FY2025; a conservative dollar-for-dollar removal from OE reduces base value by approximately $421.5 million, $2.75 per share, and the buy-below level by approximately $1.93
audit_findings.mechanism: Noncash amortization increases net sales and parent earnings; if not reversed, it enters anchor OE and is grown and terminalized.
audit_findings.evidence: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, we amortized $ 30 million, $ 30 million and $ 3 million, respectively, of the Supply Contract liability into net sales.
audit_findings.explanation: Treatment remains unverified, but even the conservative upper-bound calculation treats the full pre-tax $30 million as after-tax OE and removes it from every forecast year. The resulting $1.93 buy-below reduction is well below the $11.24 gap between market price and the stated buy-below level, so this finding alone cannot change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $30 million amortization through the FY2025 OE bridge, reverse it if included, confirm that actual unfavorable contract cash economics remain captured, and document that no double count exists.

audit_findings.title: A finite tax credit may have been capitalized in perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: $42 million of FY2025 45Q income; conservatively removing the full amount from all forecast and terminal OE reduces base value by approximately $590.1 million, $3.86 per share, and the buy-below level by approximately $2.70
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary 45Q income is embedded in aggregate anchor OE and therefore carried into forecast growth and the perpetual terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The 45Q Tax Credits are available for a 12-year period beginning on the date carbon capture and sequestration facilities are placed into service.
audit_findings.explanation: The finite 12-year life is demonstrated. However, the conservative scale test removes the entire $42 million immediately even though the Donaldsonville credits remain available into approximately 2037. That upper-bound $2.70 buy-below effect is substantially below the $11.24 price-to-buy-below gap, so the finding does not independently change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Separate 45Q income from operating OE, model each project's statutory 12-year credit period and any recapture exposure, set terminal 45Q income to zero, and confirm the valuation change remains within the conservative bound.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $64 million in FY2016 and $26 million in FY2017; $0 current valuation impact because neither year determines the $1,723.2 million FY2025 latest-actual anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially eligible D&A remains expensed in historical OE, which could raise OE if later supported as a non-economic add-back.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2016 $64.0m (9.4% of filed D&A); FY2017 $26.0m (2.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is conservative, and the cited residuals occur only in FY2016 and FY2017. Because the valuation explicitly uses FY2025 latest actual rather than a historical trend, those amounts do not enter the anchor, forecast or bridge and cannot affect the current conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Retain the conservative treatment; classify the residuals only if filed evidence becomes available, and rerun only if the anchor methodology later uses those historical years or an unidentified FY2025 residual is established.
